brief: Tech companies are increasingly funding AI capex through debt issuance, turning the AI buildout into a bond-supply story alongside an equity story. JPMorgan estimates US tech net bond issuance reaches roughly $335bn in 2026 (from $140bn), European tech issuance also accelerates, and combined tech net issuance rises about $260bn this year, inside a broader US investment-grade surge from $615bn to near $1tr. Against a $4.9tr global bond market, JPMorgan's model puts the yield impact at only 10-15bp (5-10bp after adjusting for policy-rate expectations), so the firm says this justifies AI contributing to higher yields but not an outright bond short. The more interesting signal is credit-equity divergence: CDS on AI-linked issuers has widened, and repriced more than equity volatility, while equities stay resilient and implied vol stays compressed. JPMorgan's preferred expression is not shorting bonds but buying equity convexity: three-to-six-month NDX put spreads, and favoring capital-light AI beneficiaries over capex-heavy builders.
